transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Blocked spray-arm jets, or an arm being stopped by a tall item, are the next likely causes. 1. Switch the dishwasher off and let it cool. Pull out the lower rack, twist/lift out the filter in the bottom and rinse it thoroughly under the tap. Remove any trapped food or labels from the filter well. If it is dirty, that strongly fits the symptom. 2. Check both spray arms turn freely by hand. Remove them only if they unclip easily, rinse them, and clear blocked jet holes with a wooden cocktail stick—especially any with seeds or grit in them. Do not use a metal pin, which can damage the holes. A blocked or stationary arm gives poor washing, often worse in one area. 3. Before the next wash, make sure no tall tray, pan handle or utensil can prevent either arm from spinning, and use a normal or intensive programme rather than Quick/Eco for dried-on food. Then run a normal wash with detergent. If it still leaves grit despite a clean filter and clear, freely turning arms, the next distinction is whether it is actually spraying strongly during the wash; weak/no spray can point to a water-fill or wash-circulation fault and is usually an engineer job.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok will try the filter n spray arms. filter is rank, full of food n grease. upper arm is stiff to turn, lower one spins ok. also its been on quick 30 min wash mostly

The dirty filter is very likely the main reason grit is being left behind: food can be carried back around the wash water. The stiff upper arm is also important, as it can leave the top rack poorly washed if its jets are blocked or it is catching. 1. With the dishwasher switched off, thoroughly rinse the filter and clean food/grease from the filter well. Refit it securely.
2. Take off the upper spray arm only if it unclips easily. Rinse it through and clear each small jet hole with a wooden cocktail stick; check for trapped debris and make sure it is not cracked, loose or rubbing on a basket or tall item. It should turn freely once refitted.
3. Run a normal or intensive wash rather than Quick 30, with detergent. Quick cycles are fine for lightly soiled items, but are often not enough for dried-on food or a full load. If the upper arm remains stiff after its holes are clear and nothing is catching it, the likely issue is the upper spray arm or its mounting/bearing rather than the filter alone.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did the upper arm, several holes were blocked with seeds n limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick. cleaned filter too. ran a normal wash and its much better now

That points clearly to the blocked upper spray-arm jets and dirty filter, with the Quick 30 programme not helping on heavier loads. No part is indicated if it is now washing properly. To keep it that way, rinse the filter regularly, check the spray-arm holes if results start slipping, and save Quick 30 for lightly soiled dishes; use Normal/Intensive for dried-on food or fuller loads.
